messages.author: ed01a6cf33361118
messages.subject: Units Specified
parts:
Hi,
 
I am working on hierarchical models in Unmarked to examine landscape features affecting lek density.  I ran my models (with a half-normal detection function) for 3 different model sets without specifying units. I then ran all possible combinations of the top models from each model set and then specified the units (square kilometers) for each of the models.  However, when I ran all the same models specifying square kilometers for the units the first time around, my top models changed quite a bit. I'm not sure which way to do it--specify the units for the models initially and go with those top models or run all the models firstly without specifying units and then specify units for the top models?  I'm also not sure why the top-ranked models would change so much with the units specified?  Any thoughts or suggestions would be greatly appreciated--thanks!
 
Jennifer

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Units Specified
parts:
Hi Jennifer, 

What model are you using? I'm guessing distsamp or gdistsamp. Can you show some code and output to illustrate the problem? Notice that AIC is unaffected by the "unitsOut" argument when continuing with the distsamp example:

> example(distsamp)
> fm1

Call:
distsamp(formula = ~1 ~ 1, data = ltUMF)

Density:
 Estimate    SE     z P(>|z|)
   -0.171 0.134 -1.28   0.201

Detection:
 Estimate    SE    z  P(>|z|)
     2.39 0.127 18.7 2.46e-78

AIC: 164.7524 


> update(fm1, unitsOut="kmsq")

Call:
distsamp(formula = ~1 ~ 1, data = ltUMF, unitsOut = "kmsq")

Density:
 Estimate    SE    z   P(>|z|)
     4.43 0.134 33.1 6.82e-241

Detection:
 Estimate    SE    z  P(>|z|)
     2.39 0.127 18.7 2.45e-78

AIC: 164.7524 


Richard

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Units Specified
parts:
Hi Jennifer, 

optim sometimes fails to find the maximum likelihood estimates when they are far from the starting values, as in your example. So it's always a good idea to try different starting values until you feel confident that you have found the global optima of the the likelihood. Its also a good idea to standardize your covariates. Did you do that? 

Richard
